clue.text: Journalist with a human face?

parts.note: a face is made of facial parts, so a newspaper person in charge of the human-interest section is pictured as the one in charge of a face

explanation.surface: A question about a reporter who has a kindly human side.
explanation.walkthrough: Facial features make up a face; a newspaper's features are its longer human-interest pieces, and the journalist in charge of them runs that section.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper journalist who commissions and oversees the paper's longer magazine-style articles holds this job title.

clue.text: Object of crash course study?

parts.note: a crash course is normally a quick intensive lesson, but here it is the course of an aircraft crash, which investigators study through the cockpit data box

explanation.surface: A question about what students cram for in a short intensive class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crash course' looks like rapid learning; read literally, it is the path of a crash, which air accident investigators reconstruct from the aircraft's black box.
explanation.definitionFit: Investigators of an air disaster analyse the black box that logs an aircraft's instruments and cockpit sound.

clue.text: Sailor right put off in brief

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common crossword sailor

indicators.note: off signals that the letters of put are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaman, rightly annoyed, explains himself in a few words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like 'postponed' but signals the rearrangement; 'in' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe speech or manner that is short and curt.

clue.text: Not the sole part of the shoe

definitions.text: Not the sole part of the shoe

parts.words: Not the sole part of the shoe
parts.note: the sole is the bottom of a shoe, so the part that is not the sole is the leather covering the top of the foot; 'sole' also tempts as 'only'

explanation.surface: A remark that there is more to footwear than one component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not the sole part' reads as 'not the only part', but sole is the underside of the shoe, and the rest of it above the sole has its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoemakers name the top section of a shoe, everything above the bottom, by this word.

clue.text: Look at the unattractive place. Certain things pass through it

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
a hole is slang for a dismal, unpleasant place to live

explanation.surface: Someone surveys a grim spot, adding that some things go through it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is deliberately vague: laces, threads or light pass through such an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A small opening such as a lace hole in a boot lets cord or thread go through.

clue.text: See 1
Pie not cooked after a month? It's an illusion

parts.note: DEC is the short form of December

indicators.note: an uncooked pie is in a raw, unsettled state, so the letters of pie and not are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone notices the pie is raw after a month and decides it is all a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not cooked' is the anagram signal, and 'after' puts the month first; the surface's 'a month' reads as time passing, not as an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A trick that misleads the eye or mind is a kind of false impression.

clue.text: Novel character collects paintings with new sharpness

indicators.note: collects means the outer piece gathers the other letters inside itself

parts.note: Tess is the heroine of Thomas Hardy's novel Tess of the d'Urbervilles
paintings collectively are art

explanation.surface: A fictional heroine gathers pictures with a fresh acidity.
explanation.walkthrough: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is a Thomas Hardy novel; 'collects' tells the heroine's name to hold the other letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sourness or acidity of taste, and also biting severity of words, can both be called keenness or acerbity.

clue.text: The slimmer's chemical substances

parts.note: someone losing weight is cutting down, so slimming aids could be described by the chemists' term for substances that donate electrons

explanation.surface: A dieter's pills or powders.
explanation.walkthrough: A slimmer is reducing, so the dieter's chemicals become the chemistry term for substances that bring about reduction, the opposite of oxidising ones.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, compounds that donate electrons to another substance carry this name, and a slimmer is someone shedding weight.

clue.text: Rider, put out, entered vie lently

indicators.note: put out suggests something is disturbed and upset, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An annoyed horseman barged in with force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' does double duty in the surface only: 'put' is fodder with RIDER, and 'out' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst in suddenly and forcibly, as a crowd or army might, is the sense.

clue.text: Main centre in society died, having made a point?

indicators.note: in places the central piece between the two letters

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
the core of something is its main central part

explanation.surface: A leading figure at the heart of society has died after making his point.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition has a question mark because scoring in a game means making a point, a goal or a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting a goal, run or point in a game is what this word reports.

clue.text: The powder found in the hospital cupboard

indicators.note: found in tells the solver the letters lie inside the following words

explanation.surface: A tin of dusting powder kept in a ward's storage cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' marks the run hidden across hospitAL Cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft mineral ground fine and used as a body dusting powder.

clue.text: The conic section her Poly BA involved

indicators.note: involved means twisted up and entangled, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A student's polytechnic degree course covers curves from cones.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'Poly BA' is a degree from a British polytechnic; 'involved' signals the rearrangement of all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Slicing a cone with a plane steeper than its side gives this open two-branched curve, one of the classic geometry curves.

clue.text: Name one wearing headgear back-to front causing terror

indicators.note: wearing means the letters go inside, as a head inside a cap
worn back to front means the cap is turned round, its letters read backwards

parts.note: a cap is a piece of headgear
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A person with a cap on backwards frightens everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-to front' turns CAP into PAC, and 'wearing' puts N and I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden overwhelming fear that spreads through a crowd is the sense.

clue.text: Cut standard English

parts.note: par is the normal standard or level

explanation.surface: Someone trims the textbook version of the language.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim away the skin or edge of something with a knife is to shave it down.

clue.text: Complete change of policy on stage performance

parts.note: on in the sense 'concerning' means about
a turn is a single act in a variety show

explanation.surface: A politician reverses course in a speech on theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'turn' is a music-hall or variety act. 'on' must be read as 'about the subject of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A military order to face the opposite way gives the figurative sense of reversing a stance entirely.

clue.text: Borders in study in rich colour

indicators.note: in puts the borders inside the study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
rims are borders or edges

explanation.surface: Edges of a room decorated in a deep red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con' is an old word for studying a text closely.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep purplish-red hue is the shade meant.

clue.text: See 1
Talked at length about poor player?

definitions.text: Talked at length about poor player?

parts.words: Talked at length about poor player?
parts.note: to rabbit on is British slang for chattering endlessly, and a rabbit is also a weak player in cricket or golf

explanation.surface: Someone droned on about a useless sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'rabbit' means to chatter on, and also names a poor player at cricket, tennis or golf, so the past tense of chattering looks like having discussed such a player.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this verb for going on and on in conversation, in the past tense.

clue.text: Buffet or a menu giving delight

indicators.note: to buffet is to knock about, so the letters are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: A buffet spread or a set menu brings pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' looks like a meal but is the verb meaning to knock about, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm or captivate someone so they fall in love is to please them deeply.

clue.text: Dissenter loses heart in the dance

indicators.note: loses heart means the middle letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a rebel is one who dissents from authority

explanation.surface: A protester grows discouraged on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' drops the central B of REBEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Scottish or Irish folk step danced in sets is named so.

clue.text: Drink to aim for, nothing less

indicators.note: less means the letter is taken away

parts.note: to point is to aim
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A drinker has a target, but is refused his glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes O, nothing, from POINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure of beer, roughly half a litre, is the drink ordered in British pubs.

clue.text: Seen in the ring — rock mostly paid with difficulty

indicators.note: with difficulty suggests the letters are wrenched into a new arrangement
mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: taken as written, then trimmed

explanation.surface: A boxer in the ring was paid with some trouble, by a rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims ROCK to ROC, and 'with difficulty' mixes ROC with PAID. The ring is the bullring, not a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A mounted lancer in a bullfight goads the bull from horseback in the arena.

clue.text: The women's organisation meal is pretty extensive

parts.note: the WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women
a dish is a meal or course

explanation.surface: A Women's Institute supper is rather large.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI, Women's Institute, is a British countrywide club for women, known for jam and baking.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather broad, fairly far across, is the sense of this adjective with its -ish ending.

clue.text: See 8
Old king's part in the revolution

parts.note: R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king
a bit is a part of something

explanation.surface: A former monarch played his role in the uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' means one circuit round a body, not a rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: One full circuit of a planet round the sun is a path round it.

clue.text: Putting in middle of fence and then failing

indicators.note: middle of means the inner letters of fence are taken

parts.note: failing means losing

explanation.surface: A gardener puts up the centre of a fence and then it collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes ENC from fENCe.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing something inside a cover, such as a letter in an envelope, is the sense.

clue.text: Get round tree to produce a certain view

parts.note: O is round in shape
a pine is a tree

explanation.surface: Walk round a conifer for a particular vista.
explanation.walkthrough: 'view' means opinion, not a landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: To state that you hold some opinion is to express one's thought.

clue.text: Route changed to a degree to make this?

definitions.text: Route changed to a degree to make this?

indicators.note: changed means the letters of route are put in another order

explanation.surface: A road altered slightly forces a diversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges ROUTE to DETOU, then D for degree follows; the whole clue describes a road diversion.
explanation.definitionFit: A road changed somewhat leaves drivers with a roundabout way.

clue.text: Extra sum could involve it

definitions.meaning: something extra is an added item
a school sum might be an exercise in adding up numbers

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is an added item; the second is the arithmetic operation a sum may call for.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an added extra and the arithmetic of totting up numbers share this word.

clue.text: Former Yorkshire division's hunting gear?

parts.note: Yorkshire was once split into three administrative areas called ..., so trousers worn on horseback for hunting look like clothing belonging to one of those areas

explanation.surface: A question about the outfit of an old Yorkshire region's hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire, an English county, was divided into North, East and West Ridings until 1974. Hunters on horseback wear trousers named after riding.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-fitting trousers worn on horseback, gripping at the knee, suit the hunt.

clue.text: See 29
